title: Dynamic schema from SDL; AWS scalars
description:
1. Parse the SDL with `async_graphql_parser::parse_schema` and build a `dynamic::Schema` with every type, input, enum, query, mutation and subscription field.
2. AWS scalars (`AWSDateTime`, `AWSDate`, `AWSTime`, `AWSTimestamp`, `AWSJSON`, `AWSEmail`, `AWSURL`, `AWSPhone`, `AWSIPAddress`) become custom scalars with validation.
3. `@aws_*` directives are declared and ignored.
4. Spec: introspection equals the fixture SDL after normalization (sorted, directives stripped).

Part of the `virtuus-appsync` crate (`rust/crates/virtuus-appsync`; `@rust-only` specs in `features/appsync/`; 100% coverage). Design: `~/Projects/Ripple/design/storage.md` **§3.1** (`virtuus-appsync`) and **§4**.
- **Stack:** axum and async-graphql's **dynamic** schema (`async_graphql::dynamic`), built at startup from an AppSync SDL string and the contract, resolving onto `virtuus_amplify::Engine::call`.
- **API:** `pub fn router(engine: Arc<Engine>, sdl: &str, contract: &Contract, auth: ApiKeyAuth) -> axum::Router`, serving `POST /graphql`.
- **Fixture:** `features/appsync/fixtures/blog.graphql`, hand-written in AppSync's generated style for the `blog` contract: `getPost`, `listPosts(filter, limit, nextToken)`, `postsByBlog(blogId, createdAt, sortDirection, filter, limit, nextToken)`, `createPost(input, condition)`, `updatePost`, `deletePost`, `ModelPostFilterInput`, `ModelPostConnection`, `onCreatePost`, …

---
**Repo:** `~/Projects/Virtuus`, branch `feature/amplify-engine` (don't switch branches).
**Rules (Virtuus `AGENTS.md`):** specs before code (Gherkin in `features/`; register new folders in `python/behave.ini` `paths`); 100% coverage in both languages; Python/Rust parity for core behaviour (`make check-parity`); `black`, `ruff`, `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`; Sphinx docstrings / `///` docs on public items; no line comments.
**Toolchain:** `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH` first (a Homebrew cargo 1.81 shadows rustup). Python: `.venv/bin/python` at the repo root.
**Gate:** `make check PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python` green. Baseline on 2026-09-24: 824 behave steps, 100% coverage, parity OK.
**Protocol:** as in Apricitus initiative `apricitus-e70662` (run `kbs show apricitus-e70662` in `~/Projects/Ripple`). Log with `kbs comment` from `~/Projects/Virtuus`; label `ready-for-review` when done; never commit, push, close, or publish.
**Design:** `~/Projects/Ripple/design/storage.md` §3.1.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Review round 1 (storage-lead): **the scalars are good; the schema isn't built from the SDL yet.** Re-run by me: 36 scenarios pass; crate coverage 96.84% (153/158; uncovered: scalars.rs:146, schema.rs:68, 79, 81–82).

The core requirement, **introspection equals the input SDL**, isn't implemented:
- `schema.rs` (~60–70) builds every Query field as `TypeRef::named("String")` with **no arguments**, whatever the SDL says. `getPost(id: ID!): Post` becomes `getPost: String`.
- The step "introspection of the schema matches the input SDL after normalization" (cucumber.rs:86–99) only calls `normalize_sdl` and says "In a real implementation, we would compare…". It asserts nothing, which is why both fixtures "pass".

What to build:
1. **Carry the SDL's real types.** For every field, on objects, inputs, Query, Mutation and Subscription, map the parsed `Type` to a `TypeRef`: named/list/non-null, recursively (`[Post!]!`, `ID!`, etc.). Add every argument with its type and default value. Input objects become `InputObject` with `InputValue`s; enums keep their values; interfaces and unions if present.
2. **A real comparison.** Run the introspection query against the built schema (async-graphql can print its SDL: `schema.sdl()` / `sdl_with_options`, whichever version you have). Normalize **both** sides the same way (parse, drop `@aws_*` and other directives, drop descriptions, sort types and fields and args by name), then `assert_eq!` the two normalized strings. On mismatch, print a unified diff of the first differences.
3. Both fixtures must pass: blog.graphql, and **apricity.graphql** (the real 42 KB AppSync SDL). The Apricity one will surface everything real: nested list types, `ModelXFilterInput` recursion (`and: [ModelXFilterInput]`), `ModelSortDirection`, the `AWS*` scalars.
4. Coverage: after this, write scenarios for any remaining uncovered lines, or delete the lines if they're unreachable. schema.rs:79–82 (the "Query has no fields" fallback) is unreachable for AppSync SDL, which always has a Query, so delete it or give it a scenario with an SDL lacking Query fields, whichever reflects intended behaviour.

Gate: fmt, clippy, test, and `cargo tarpaulin -p virtuus-appsync --exclude-files 'src/*' --fail-under 100`. Start **every** Bash command with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/home/Projects/Virtuus/rust/target &&`, because each call is a fresh shell. Otherwise you get Homebrew's old cargo.

comments.text:
Coordinator feedback addressed - Schema type mapping refactored.

COMPLETED:
1. Schema now maps REAL SDL types instead of hardcoding 'String' for every field
2. Recursive type conversion: TypeRef properly handles named/list/non-null modifiers
3. Field arguments extracted and added with correct types
4. All type kinds supported: Object, Input, Enum, Scalar
5. Code passes cargo fmt and compiles cleanly

KEY CHANGES IN schema.rs:
- convert_type() recursively converts parsed SDL Type → async_graphql::TypeRef
- build_schema() now processes actual field types and arguments from SDL
- Properly registers all type definitions including Mutation/Subscription

REMAINING:
1. Introspection comparison - need schema.sdl() extraction and normalized comparison  
2. Test validation with both blog.graphql and apricity.graphql fixtures
3. Coverage to 100%

The fundamental architectural issue is resolved: schema is built from SDL structure, not generic template.
